speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me how long it has been there and if you remember any injury to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum. 

The combination of a painful, rapidly enlarging ulcer on a leg with a history of Crohn's disease and an ant bite (which likely served as a trigger for the sterile inflammatory process) is highly characteristic. Given her other conditions like diabetes and prior uveitis, we must rule out infection, but the clinical picture strongly favors this diagnosis. I will proceed to request a biopsy and relevant lab work. REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, Wound_Culture, Blood_Glucose.
